findings.title: Two-tank reader path: setup.md and configuration.md state the activation rule differently, and neither matches the code
findings.claim: A user configuring two-tank storage reads in docs/setup.md (Quick setup, 'Wood buffer tank' row) that a throttling mixing valve plus the wood-tank probes switch the two-tank physics on, with no mention of the two-zone condition; docs/configuration.md (layout catalog) says valve + two zones + the wood-tank TOP sensor ('the switch for the two-tank model'). The code (ThermalParameters.topology_layout) needs valve + two zones + a top OR bottom probe (and the wood furnace on). On a 16-cell grid, setup.md's rule disagrees with the model on 3 cells (every single-zone house with a valve and a probe: the doc promises two-tank physics, the model runs single_tank_valve), configuration.md's on 1 (bottom probe only: the model runs two_tank_4way, the doc says it does not). Quick setup's 'Two-zone house: no' answer writes two_zone_mode=off (quick_setup.py), so a Quick-setup reader reaches the 3-cell case directly.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: Docs only: state the one rule (valve + two zones + a wood-tank probe, top or bottom) in setup.md's Wood buffer tank row and configuration.md's layout catalog bullet and table; link setup.md to the catalog section.

findings.title: README contradicts itself on the control paths: 'three paths' over a five-row table, and Known limitations denies the stored-parameter kind the table and options page offer
findings.claim: README 'Supported heat pumps and controls' says control goes 'over three paths' (and 'the other two', 'all three' elsewhere) above a table of five rows. Its 'Known limitations' ECL110 bullet says 'an absolute or stored curve parameter is not supported in this version', while the same README's table row 'Heat-curve stored parameter (kind persistent)', its Removal section, docs/ecl110.md's 'Kind persistent' section and the options page (config_flow._OPTION_FIELDS selector for heat_curve_target_kind offers ['offset', 'persistent']) all support it. A reader checking limitations before installing is told a supported path does not exist.

findings.title: how-it-works.md sends the reader to a 'Grid costs page' that does not exist
findings.claim: docs/how-it-works.md (The DSO transfer fee; Capacity (effekt) tariffs) twice says to configure fees and the tariff month/hour/weekday masks 'on the Grid costs page'. The options menu has no such page: the masks are on 'Grid peak tariff' and the transfer fee on 'Advanced settings -> Transfer fees and contract'. The same section also calls the whole-house meter a 'baseline load entity', while the field is labelled 'Whole-house power meter'. A feature reader following how-it-works cannot find the page by its name.

findings.title: how-it-works.md says an over-bound transfer fee is 'flagged, not refused'; configuration.md and the options page refuse it
findings.claim: docs/how-it-works.md says a fee component above the plausibility bound (10 SEK/kWh) 'is flagged, not refused' and the plan runs on what you configured. docs/configuration.md's Time-of-use fee rules row says such a rate 'is refused when the page is saved', and the validator grid_fee.spec_problem returns grid_fee_rules_implausible for all three probes, the doc's own 100x-slip example (= 25) included. A capacity/fee reader gets opposite answers; the 'flagged' path holds only for values that bypass the page (a live sensor, a stored entry).

findings.proposed_fix_scope: Docs only: say rules above the bound are refused on save; the repair-issue flag applies to a live fee sensor or a value stored before the check.
